### Context

A local test that refreshes the account page turns the saved dark theme into light. Switching off the later default-theme step kept dark.

### What is broken

After a refresh, the account page shows the light theme even though the saved choice is dark.

### Why it is broken

Two steps set the theme on the account page. The page first loads the saved choice, dark, from the user's stored profile. A separate step that applies the standard theme then runs and replaces it with light.

### How to fix it

Skip the standard-theme step once a saved theme has loaded, so a refresh keeps dark. This changes one small step. Choose hotfix because the change is small and passes every safety check.

### What is broken

Refreshing the account page resets the saved dark theme to light instead of keeping the saved choice.

### Why it is broken

The page first applies the saved dark theme returned by the service that stores profile settings. A separate step then applies the default light theme, overwriting that choice. The local test reproduced dark becoming light; disabling the later default-setting step kept dark.

### How to fix it

Skip default initialization once a saved theme has loaded, so refreshing retains dark instead of resetting to light. This is a small change to the default-setting step. Choose hotfix because the change is bounded and the failing action can be tested.

### What is broken

Refreshing the account page resets the saved dark theme to light.

### Why it is broken

Two parts of the page set the theme: the profile loader applies the saved `"dark"` value, then the default-theme initializer overwrites it with `"light"` (`src/profile-theme.ts:62`). The local test `node --test test/profile-theme.test.mjs` reproduces the reset; disabling the later initializer keeps dark, supporting the overwrite as the cause.

### How to fix it

Skip default initialization after a saved theme has loaded so refresh retains dark. This is a small, bounded change to the initializer, with the existing local test covering the failure. Choose hotfix because the fix is small and all six eligibility predicates pass.

The one regression is concision: the How to fix it section repeats itself and echoes the menu - 'This is a small, bounded change to the initializer' restates 'small', and 'Choose hotfix because the fix is small and all six eligibility predicates pass' duplicates both the recommended=3 marker and the 'eligible - all predicates pass' line. anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the sectioned contract cleanly: the four ### headings carry whole sentences, Context is two lines with the repro and the surviving explanation, the mechanism is named by role ("a separate step that sets a default theme") with the file path trailing the claim, and How to fix it names the literal change, its one-step size, and the recommended pick with a single because-clause.
